american airlines announced on august 18, 2026, that it will install seatback screens at every seat on more than 800 narrowbody aircraft.
american expects to finish 2026 around break-even while delta and united forecast solid profits; ceo robert isom has acknowledged the performance gap.

in 2017, american decided against installing seatback screens on its incoming boeing 737 max aircraft, reasoning that over 90% of passengers brought their own devices and invested instead in streaming entertainment and faster inflight internet.
new airbus and boeing aircraft will begin arriving with the screens in 2028, when american will also start retrofitting existing fleet aircraft, with work expected to continue into the early 2030s.

the new systems will include 4k displays with bluetooth connectivity, usb-c fast charging and interactive flight maps, with premium seats receiving larger displays; american is also moving ahead with starlink high-speed wi-fi.
american airlines is adding more first class and main cabin extra seats through major fleetwide cabin upgrades.
american airlines will increase premium narrowbody seats from 25% to 40% of capacity, representing a 60% boost.
